# Crash table (generated by scripts/haven_crash_table.py; descriptive only)

Returns in percent. 'n/a' = no data for that asset on those dates. Day 0 of the
worst leg is the close before the worst 15-trading-day S&P 500 fall inside the
drawdown. Treasuries rebuilt from constant-maturity yields; FX = currency move only.
'worst point' = the asset's lowest cumulative return, measured from the equity peak,
at any close up to the trough (how far under water a holder was at the worst moment).
'own max drawdown' = the asset's own largest peak-to-trough fall inside the window.
Oslo (OBX) closes before New York, so its 1-day numbers are not the same session.

Correction 2026-11-18 (review round 1): the OBX-in-EUR column used EUR/NOK =
(NOK per USD) / (USD per EUR), which is wrong; it is now (NOK per USD) * (USD per EUR),
checked to lie in 6-15. Every OBX-in-EUR cell changed; no other column did.
